walkthroughs.body_html:
Physical Chemistry — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Physical Chemistry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Physical Chemistry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Members of a homologous series share:
options: The same molecular mass
The same functional group and general formula
The same boiling point
The same number of isomers

mcqs.q: Does a catalyst affect the position of equilibrium?
options: A catalyst shifts the equilibrium towards the products.
A catalyst increases the yield by being consumed in the forward reaction only.
A catalyst decreases Kc by stabilising the reactants.
No — it speeds up both the forward and reverse reactions equally, so equilibrium is reached faster but at the same position.

mcqs.q: Does adding a catalyst change the value of Kc?
options: A catalyst increases Kc by favouring product formation.
No — a catalyst speeds up forward and reverse reactions equally, so Kc is unchanged.
A catalyst decreases Kc by stabilising the reactants.
Heterogeneous catalysts are consumed; homogeneous catalysts are not.

mcqs.q: What distinguishes a heterogeneous from a homogeneous catalyst?
options: A catalyst decreases Kc by stabilising the reactants.
Heterogeneous catalysts are consumed; homogeneous catalysts are not.
A heterogeneous catalyst is in a different phase from the reactants; a homogeneous catalyst is in the same phase.
Heterogeneous catalysts are solid and homogeneous catalysts are liquid — full stop.
